flashcard_questions.q: What does the rhythm section of an ensemble do?
flashcard_questions.a: It keeps time and sets the groove.

flashcard_questions.q: Which instrument in a wind quintet comes from the brass family?
Which instrument is the main melodic voice of a piano trio?
Which string quartet instrument fills the inner chord parts alongside the cello?
Why does a string quartet have no dedicated rhythm section?
flashcard_questions.a: The pulse comes from articulation and bowing instead.

flashcard_questions.q: Which two instruments usually lead the melody in a big band?
flashcard_questions.a: The lead trumpet and the lead alto saxophone.

flashcard_questions.q: How many trumpets does a big band horn section typically include?
Which ensemble in this unit has a dedicated rhythm section?

flashcard_questions.a: One part plays a phrase and another part answers it.
A secondary melody played against the main melody.
A composition written for one or two instruments.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does a trio sonata not mean three players?
flashcard_questions.a: The name counts the three written parts, not the performers.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a riff in a big band?
flashcard_questions.a: A short repeated pattern played by the horn section.

flashcard_questions.q: Who wrote the music for the musical Wicked?

notes: 15 cards: 5 instrument-to-role cards across the four ensembles, 2 cause cards (no rhythm section in chamber groups, the trio sonata misconception), 4 term-to-definition (rhythm section, call-and-response, countermelody, sonata, riff), 1 big-band number card, and 2 composer cards. The four-role list and the big band line-up were split or left out so no answer is an enumeration, and the expressive-effect table was dropped because its cards would have interfering answers.
